note: Descriptive attributes proposed for the A3 Application architecture; the 11 approved common attributes apply too. Every public source was opened and checked on 2026-10-24.

attributes.name: release_version
attributes.meaning: the product release that is in use (not the version of this model record)
attributes.question: Which release of the product are we running?
attributes.reasoning: CycloneDX names the version of a component exactly this way; checked 2026-10-24. Distinct from the core `version`, which versions the architecture record.

attributes.name: license
attributes.meaning: the licence, as an SPDX identifier (e.g. Apache-2.0)
attributes.question: Which licences do we depend on, and are any restricted?
attributes.reasoning: SPDX identifiers are the public standard for naming licences and CycloneDX uses them; checked 2026-10-24.

attributes.name: cpe
attributes.meaning: the product's CPE 2.3 name, for vulnerability matching
attributes.question: Which published vulnerabilities affect this application?
attributes.reasoning: NIST's standard product naming, used to match vulnerability records; checked 2026-10-24.

attributes.name: hosting_model
attributes.question: What runs on premises and what runs in the cloud?
attributes.source: NIST SP 800-145 The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing (public)
attributes.term: service models SaaS, PaaS, IaaS (§2, PDF p.6–7)
attributes.reasoning: NIST defines the three cloud service models; checked 2026-10-24. SDEM adds `on-premises` for applications outside any cloud, so the value list is SDEM's.

attributes.name: recovery_time_objective
attributes.meaning: how quickly the application must be back after an outage (e.g. "4h")
attributes.question: How fast must this application recover?
attributes.reasoning: Defined in NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (NIST glossary); checked 2026-10-24. The resilience measure banks report, more precise than a criticality label.

attributes.name: recovery_point_objective
attributes.meaning: how much data loss is tolerable, as a time (e.g. "15m")
attributes.question: How much data can this application afford to lose?
attributes.reasoning: Defined in NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (NIST glossary); checked 2026-10-24.

attributes.name: disposition
attributes.meaning: what the bank plans to do with the application
attributes.question: Which applications do we keep, invest in, replace or retire?
attributes.reasoning: The application-rationalisation question. Published classifications are proprietary, so SDEM defines its own plain values.

attributes.name: contract_format
attributes.meaning: the format of the interface's machine-readable contract
attributes.question: Which interfaces have a machine-readable contract, and in which format?
attributes.reasoning: Each value names a public specification (checked 2026-10-24 for OpenAPI and AsyncAPI); the list itself is SDEM's.

attributes.name: security_scheme
attributes.question: How is this interface secured?
attributes.reasoning: OpenAPI defines exactly these five scheme types; checked 2026-10-24.

attributes.name: protocol
attributes.meaning: the protocol the interface uses (e.g. https, amqp, kafka, mqtt)
attributes.question: Which protocols do our interfaces use?
attributes.reasoning: AsyncAPI names protocols this way, covering both request and event interfaces; checked 2026-10-24.

attributes.name: operation_id
attributes.meaning: the operation's unique id in its API contract
attributes.question: Which contract operation is this, exactly?
attributes.reasoning: OpenAPI field; lets an export match an operation to its contract even when paths change; checked 2026-10-24.

attributes.name: deprecated
attributes.meaning: whether the operation is deprecated in its contract
attributes.question: Which API operations are being phased out?

attributes.name: personal_information
attributes.meaning: whether it holds information about an identifiable person
attributes.question: Which applications hold personal information?
attributes.source: EU GDPR Art. 4(1) and NZ Privacy Act 2020 s 7
attributes.reasoning: Same definition as the A1 and A2 business objects; public law.

attributes.name: glossary_uri
attributes.meaning: link to the agreed glossary definition
attributes.question: Which business term does this data entity hold?
attributes.reasoning: Same as the business objects: ties application data to the agreed business term.

attributes.name: system_of_record
attributes.meaning: whether this application is the authoritative source for the data
attributes.question: Where is the golden source of this data?
attributes.reasoning: A core data-architecture question; open standards do not define the field.

attributes.name: retention_period
attributes.meaning: how long the data must be kept (e.g. "7y")
attributes.question: How long must we keep this data?
attributes.reasoning: Driven by law and policy that vary by bank and country; SDEM records the period only.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.meaning: the type name the event carries (e.g. "payment.initiated")
attributes.question: Which events exist, by type?

attributes.name: event_source
attributes.meaning: the source the event identifies itself with
attributes.question: Which system emits this event?

attributes.name: schema_uri
attributes.meaning: link to the schema the event data follows
attributes.question: Where is the contract for this event?

changes.proposed: keep the name; re-source to CycloneDX components[].supplier (public, checked 2026-10-24) → high
changes.reasoning: The meaning is the same as CycloneDX's supplier; the examples already use it ("in-house", a synthetic supplier). Renaming would break exports for no gain.

derived.name: criticality
derived.rule: the highest criticality of the A1 processes whose Service Domains the application realises (USES_DOMAIN then REALIZED_BY)
derived.reasoning: Same choice as A2: derived, so it cannot drift; RTO and RPO carry the stored resilience values.

decisions: **The three SDEM-defined attributes** (`disposition`, `system_of_record`, `retention_period`). *Recommended: keep all three* — rationalisation, golden source and retention are among the most-asked questions and no open standard covers them.
**`vendor`**. *Recommended: keep the name and re-source it to CycloneDX `supplier` (high).*
**Application criticality**. *Recommended: derive it (DV-A3-01) and store RTO/RPO instead*, consistent with the A2 decision.
**Required attributes**. *Recommended: none required* — exports from portfolio tools vary; the completeness warnings report gaps without rejecting data.
decisions_taken: vendor keeps its name, re-sourced to CycloneDX components[].supplier (high)
application criticality derived (DV-A3-01); RTO and RPO stored
